lines.text: For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. Of Asaph.
Sing for joy to God our strength;
make a joyful noise to the God of Jacob.
Lift up a song, strike the tambourine,
play the sweet-sounding harp and lyre.
Sound the ram’s horn at the New Moon,
and at the full moon on the day of our Feast.
For this is a statute for Israel,
an ordinance of the God of Jacob.
He ordained it as a testimony for Joseph
when he went out over the land of Egypt,
where I heard an unfamiliar language:

pictures.scene: Anders Zorn, Midsommardans — the whole village swung round in the dance on the long summer evening, for the choirmaster according to Gittith of Asaph, sing for joy to God our strength
pictures.name: pd_zorn_midsommardans

pictures.scene: Hendrick ter Brugghen, Bagpipe Player — the piper leaning into his instrument with his whole breath, make a joyful noise to the God of Jacob
pictures.name: pd_brugghen_doedelzak

pictures.scene: Orazio Gentileschi, The Lute Player — the player bent over the strings with the music open before her, lift up a song strike the tambourine, play the sweet-sounding harp and lyre
pictures.name: pd_gentileschi_lute_player

pictures.scene: Francisco Goya, La pradera de San Isidro — the whole city gone out to keep its feast day in the open meadow, sound the ram's horn at the New Moon
pictures.name: pd_goya_san_isidro

pictures.scene: Solomon Alexander Hart, The Feast of the Rejoicing of the Law — the scrolls carried up through the crowded synagogue on the appointed day, and at the full moon on the day of our Feast, for this is a statute for Israel
pictures.name: pd_hart_rejoicing_law

pictures.scene: Frederick Goodall, Subsiding the Nile — the river country of Egypt with its people and beasts at the water, an ordinance of the God of Jacob, He ordained it as a testimony for Joseph
pictures.name: pd_goodall_subsiding_nile
